title: Linear-time directed shortest paths with nonnegative real weights
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic comparison-addition algorithm computing all exact distances from a specified source in every directed graph with arbitrary nonnegative real arc lengths in \(O(m+n)\) worst-case time?
definitions: The graph is given by its vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) arcs. It has no loops and at most one arc per ordered pair; opposite arcs are allowed. Each arc length belongs to \(\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\). The length of a path is the sum of its arc lengths; the empty path has length zero. Output the minimum source-to-vertex path length for every vertex, with an infinity marker for unreachable vertices. Zero-length arcs and cycles are permitted. Use a uniform comparison-addition RAM. Real cells contain exact real numbers and support copying, addition, subtraction and comparison at unit cost; fixed rational program constants are allowed. Real multiplication, division, floor, bit extraction and conversion of an input-dependent real to an integer are not primitives. Integer control and address words have \(d\lceil\log_{2}(n+2)\rceil\) bits for a fixed constant \(d\), with unit-cost Boolean operations, shifts, comparison and arithmetic on words. Integer operations cannot inspect real encodings. A fixed finite program receives no advice or free tables. Memory accesses, control, preprocessing and output all count. Bounds are uniform over all real edge values. The algorithm must halt correctly on every input without randomness, with a universal time constant.

context_blocks.text: Reading a graph and writing its source distances already requires linear time. The question asks whether arbitrary nonnegative real lengths and direction can be handled within that exact input-and-output budget.
Duan and coauthors broke the sorting barrier in 2025. The 2026 improvement gives \(O(m\sqrt{\log n}+\sqrt{mn\log n\log\log n})\) time, still with superlinear overhead.
Exact reals can be added and compared, while their bit representations cannot be inspected. This makes the model substantive: integer bit operations do not supply a real-weight algorithm.
Mareš develops the shortest-path background. The present endpoint follows the newer directed real-weight results rather than treating historical textbook bounds as current.

why: An optimal linear algorithm would determine whether directed shortest paths with general nonnegative numerical lengths can be computed at the cost of reading the graph.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

sentences: The input is a directed graph with arbitrary nonnegative real arc lengths and a specified source.
The task is to output every exact source distance.
The question asks for deterministic linear worst-case time using real addition and comparison.
Recent algorithms break the sorting barrier while retaining superlinear overhead.
A linear algorithm would match the cost of reading the graph and writing the distances.
